metaData.originalTitle: AI Agent 如何重构 App 稳定性治理流程
metaData.title: How AI Agents Are Reshaping App Stability Governance
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically describes the App Stability Analysis Agent built by the Baidu Maps team, which uses a Tool + Workflow architecture and a RAG data flywheel to achieve end-to-end processing from crash log parsing to automatic repair.
metaData.summary: This article provides a detailed introduction to the Stability Analysis Agent project open-sourced by the Baidu Maps development platform. It aims to address common pain points in traditional App stability governance, such as long troubleshooting chains, heavy reliance on expert experience, and high cross-team collaboration costs. The core solution is to build a unified Agent framework that integrates toolchain automation with AI-powered intelligent analysis. The framework is centered around extensible Tools (atomic capabilities like log parsing, address symbolication, and code extraction) and Workflows (scenario-specific strategies like Crash analysis), adopting a multi-shell architecture (CLI/Daemon/IDE Plugin). Currently, it has implemented an automated Crash analysis scenario, enabling end-to-end processing from crash log parsing, address symbolication, and code context extraction to AI reasoning and fix suggestions. The article also provides an in-depth comparison of this Agent versus directly using AI coding tools or developing Skills, emphasizing the 'data flywheel' effect achieved through a vector database-driven RAG knowledge base, which makes the system smarter with use. Furthermore, it shares challenges encountered during engineering implementation, such as intelligent source code location and precise function body extraction, and outlines a roadmap for covering ANR, lag, and memory governance in the future.

mainPoints.point: Build a unified Agent framework to orchestrate the entire stability analysis process.
mainPoints.explanation: By using a layered Tool + Workflow architecture, atomic capabilities like log parsing, address symbolication, and code extraction are decoupled from scenario-specific analysis strategies, creating an automated closed loop from evidence collection to reasoning output.

mainPoints.point: Introduce a vector database-driven RAG knowledge base to create a data flywheel.
mainPoints.explanation: Structured evidence and fix strategies from each analysis are deposited into a knowledge base. New issues can quickly reuse historical experience through rule matching and semantic retrieval, making the analysis of similar problems increasingly accurate and turning experience into organizational assets.

mainPoints.point: The Agent holds a fundamental advantage over AI coding tools or Skills.
mainPoints.explanation: AI coding tools cannot execute toolchain operations and suffer from noisy logs; Skills lack persistent knowledge accumulation and deterministic guarantees. The Agent, through deterministic toolchain orchestration, structured intermediate artifacts, and a RAG knowledge base, simultaneously addresses both toolchain and knowledge accumulation challenges.

keyQuotes: Traditional manual troubleshooting processes are inefficient and heavily reliant on experts. This solution builds a unified Agent framework by combining toolchain automation with AI-powered intelligent analysis.
By introducing a vector database-driven RAG knowledge base, the system can accumulate processing experience, achieving a 'data flywheel' effect where it gets smarter with use.
AI coding tools lack toolchains and context, while AI platform Skills lack knowledge accumulation and deterministic guarantees—the Agent possesses the advantages of both.

The value of an Agent lies not just in 'analyzing accurately this time,' but more importantly in 'being faster and more accurate next time.' This is the significance of the vector database-driven data flywheel.

relatedArticles.title: Is Your Skill Up to Standard?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes an 8-dimensional quantitative evaluation framework for AI Agent Skills, covering metrics such as metadata quality, execution guidance, and domain knowledge density to assign ratings, and designs a multi-model cross-validation process and four execution strategies to enhance the reliability and compatibility of the assessment.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: After Reading the Claude Code Source Code, I Realized: The Differences Between Skills, MCP, and Rules Are Not as Big as You Think
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article, through an in-depth analysis of the leaked Claude Code source code, reveals the underlying implementation mechanisms of the three concepts—Rules, MCP, and Skills—pointing out that their core difference lies in where information is injected within the API request, and provides practical advice based on insights from the source code.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Enabling Coding Agents to Reliably Complete Long-Horizon Tasks
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article introduces the Harness Engineering framework, which addresses the reliability challenges of Coding Agents in large-scale, long-horizon tasks through task decomposition, parallel scheduling, File-as-Progress state persistence, and multi-layered retry mechanisms.

relatedArticles.title: 2 Hours, 0 Lines of Handwritten Code: I Built a Production-Grade VSCode Extension with Claude
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details the author's complete process of building a production-grade VSCode extension (for monitoring Comate AI model usage) from scratch using Claude in 2 hours, emphasizing the core value of human judgment and decision-making in human-machine collaboration.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: GPT-5.4 Released: OpenAI's First Unified Model, Truly Native
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4, creating the first unified Agent model that supports native Computer Use by integrating reasoning, coding, and computer interaction.

relatedArticles.title: Browser Use: Building a Runtime Harness for Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build an open-source tool based on the Chrome DevTools Protocol that enables AI agents to operate real browsers for multi-dimensional verification—including visual, interactive, and console checks—thereby ensuring the delivery quality of web products.
